Rather than changing it around to return an error, can we change the code that ignores the panic to catch the panic instead and cleanly shut down kubelet?

Could you share more about the benefits of using panic/defer vs returning an
error? In my, limited, experience, my sense is that the Go community prefers
returning errors, unless there's a strong reason not to. In this situation,
I believe our ability to cleanly shutdown the Kubelet should still exist if we
return an error.

Its very possible I'm missing an advantage of using panic/defer though :)

> Could you share more about the benefits of using panic/defer vs returning an error?

Heh...I'm the wrong person to be asking about what the Go community or the Kubernetes community prefers.  I was just assuming that there'd be less code churn involved.

One other thought...did you consider deleting the state file and rebuilding it if validation fails?

issue_context.title: cpumanager: kubelet should log fatal error and exit rather than panic when cpu manager fails on startup
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


**What happened**:

When static policy is enabled, cpu manager do validate state between checkpoint (`/var/lib/kubelet/cpu_manager_state`) and current node cpu topology before kubelet fully started. If the validation is failed (sometimes occurred after node or kubelet crash), cpu manager will panic immediately. However, this panic is handled and ignored by upper wait.Util(). This causes kubelet continue to start (PLEG, syncLoop) normally although other modules in container manager (like qosContainerManager, in setupNode method) doesn't start successfully. Then, kubelet sync pod with a uninitialized qosContainerManager. And it will leads to unexpected results such as:

1. panic when call UpdateQoSCgroups in syncPod.
3. all pods/containers on node will be killed
3. all cgroup path (like kubepods.slice) recursively in each cgroup will be housekept.
2. node status is still ready, kubelet process is still running (doesn't work, panic continuously but not exit)

**What you expected to happen**:

IMHO, It may not be a good idea that panics in new/start code logic. We shoud use `return err` instead, so the caller is able to check the err and exit immediately.

kubelet should log fatal error and exit when some modules create or start failed.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

1. enable cpu manager static policy

modify `/var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml` to enable cpu manager static policy:

```
cpuManagerPolicy: static
systemReserved:
  cpu: 500m
  memory: 200M
```

remove `/var/lib/kubelet/cpu_manager_state` and restart kubelet


2. modify /var/lib/kubelet/cpu_manager_state by a invalid value to simulate node crash situation.

for example, change valid checkpoint from:
```
{"policyName":"static","defaultCpuSet":"0-3","checksum":2479968155}
```
to:
```
{"policyName":"static","defaultCpuSet":"0,2-3","checksum":1104188325}
```

3. restart kubelet again

**Anything else we need to know?**:

Ref: 
1. container manager start and panic:

- container manager start: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/08410cbf06f1c8649157407c660b1c5cb528947b/pkg/kubelet/cm/container_manager_linux.go#L576

- cpu manager start: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/cm/cpumanager/cpu_manager.go#L180

- static policy panic: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/08410cbf06f1c8649157407c660b1c5cb528947b/pkg/kubelet/cm/cpumanager/policy_static.go#L122

2. it can neither catch the error nor exit immediately here:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/08410cbf06f1c8649157407c660b1c5cb528947b/pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go#L1375

This PR would Fix it, PLTA: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/84705

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/84783

Why remove the newlines here? It is usually easer to read if it is broken up, and forces it to jump out when this is the error.

I'm not 100% against the change, just curious about the reasoning to change it.

It is just friendly for log collectors which are sensitive to newline. :)
 
Single-line error message may be easy for being collected with log prefix (level, time, file and line number, etc.).  
Multi-line one might lose prefix which contains that info. When these lines are sent to remote log db and parsed to structured data, It is sometimes hard to search and locate.

Logging here is redundant because the same information is printed when the Container manager errors out at the next level based on the returned error.

I'd say it's OK for now though. Let's get this PR pushed through and then come back with a cleanup PR for these kind of things afterwards-

I wrote the patch that recently got merged that introduced this, so wanted to make sure it got covered here on the rebase :)
